notes: Current NIDDK Dermatitis Herpetiformis guidance was reread and directly supports the celiac association, intensely pruritic symmetric papulovesicles, epidermal transglutaminase autoantigen, and granular IgA deposition in upper/papillary dermis.

NCBI StatPearls Dermatitis Herpetiformis was reread for TG3 versus TG2 biology, subepidermal blistering, neutrophils at dermal papillary tips, extensor distribution, and granular IgA direct immunofluorescence.
A 2021 PubMed Central review was reread for epitope spreading from TG2-directed celiac immunity to high-affinity IgA against TG3, the main dermatitis-herpetiformis autoantigen.

NCBI sources for pemphigus vulgaris, bullous pemphigoid, and epidermolysis bullosa acquisita were reread to verify desmoglein 3, BP180/type XVII collagen, and type VII collagen as real distractor targets.
The official USMLE Content Outline 2026 explicitly lists dermatitis herpetiformis under Skin & Subcutaneous Tissue — immunologic/inflammatory — vesiculobullous disorders.

blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

claim_audit.phenotype: NIDDK and NCBI support an intensely pruritic, symmetric papulovesicular eruption concentrated on extensor elbows/knees, buttocks, back or scalp; excoriation commonly destroys intact vesicles.
claim_audit.celiac_association: Dermatitis herpetiformis is a cutaneous manifestation of gluten-sensitive enteropathy, and clinically evident gastrointestinal symptoms may be absent.
claim_audit.histology: NCBI supports subepidermal blister formation with neutrophils concentrated at dermal papillary tips.
claim_audit.immunofluorescence: NIDDK and NCBI identify granular IgA deposits in the papillary/upper dermis on direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin.
claim_audit.tg3_key: NIDDK states that IgA antibodies form against epidermal transglutaminase; NCBI and the review identify TG3 as the dominant/main autoantigen in dermatitis herpetiformis.
claim_audit.tg2_nuance: TG2 is the principal celiac-enteropathy autoantigen and anti-TG2 antibodies can coexist in dermatitis herpetiformis, so the key is deliberately phrased 'most characteristically' rather than asserting that TG3 is the only antibody target.
claim_audit.distractor_1: TG2 is a serious distractor because of the patient's gluten-sensitive disease biology, but it is not the dominant cutaneous antigen responsible for the characteristic papillary skin deposits.
claim_audit.distractor_2: Desmoglein 3 is a pemphigus vulgaris target and causes intraepidermal acantholysis rather than the granular papillary IgA pattern.
claim_audit.distractor_3: BP180/type XVII collagen is a bullous-pemphigoid hemidesmosomal target and produces linear basement-membrane immunoreactant deposition rather than granular papillary IgA.
claim_audit.distractor_4: Type VII collagen is the anchoring-fibril target in epidermolysis bullosa acquisita, not dermatitis herpetiformis.
claim_audit.blueprint_claim: The official USMLE 2026 outline explicitly names dermatitis herpetiformis in the vesiculobullous skin-disorder list.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: The extensor pruritic grouped eruption plus subepidermal vesicle, neutrophils at dermal papillary tips, and granular papillary IgA identifies dermatitis herpetiformis. The foundational distinction is that TG2 is the principal gut autoantigen in celiac disease, whereas TG3/epidermal transglutaminase is the dominant cutaneous autoantigen in dermatitis herpetiformis.
adversarial_second_pass.tg2_second_answer_challenge: Patients with dermatitis herpetiformis frequently have circulating anti-TG2 antibodies because of associated celiac autoimmunity. However, the question asks specifically about IgA in the skin and what it is most characteristically directed against; authoritative sources identify TG3 as the skin antigen and main DH autoantigen. TG2 is therefore plausible but not equally defensible.
adversarial_second_pass.linear_iga_challenge: Linear IgA bullous dermatosis can present with subepidermal blisters and IgA, but direct immunofluorescence is linear along the basement membrane rather than granular in dermal papillae, and the extensor/celiac/TG3 pattern favors dermatitis herpetiformis.
adversarial_second_pass.pemphigus_challenge: Pemphigus vulgaris usually has flaccid intraepidermal bullae, mucosal involvement and intercellular IgG against desmogleins; the tissue plane and immunofluorescence differ.
adversarial_second_pass.bullous_pemphigoid_challenge: Bullous pemphigoid produces tense subepidermal bullae and eosinophil-rich inflammation with linear IgG/C3 at the basement membrane; the patient's neutrophilic papillary/granular-IgA pattern is different.
adversarial_second_pass.eba_challenge: EBA targets type VII collagen and can form subepidermal blisters, but typically shows IgG along the dermal-epidermal junction and trauma-prone/scarring phenotypes rather than classic DH.
adversarial_second_pass.absent_gi_symptoms_challenge: Absence of chronic diarrhea or weight loss does not undermine dermatitis herpetiformis; authoritative guidance notes that gastrointestinal celiac symptoms are absent in many DH patients.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All five options are named protein antigens of comparable length and taxonomic level. The correct answer is not the only transglutaminase option; TG2 supplies a deliberately strong near-neighbor distractor.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No prevalence, antibody titer cutoff, DIF sensitivity, HLA frequency, or treatment-response interval is required to answer the item.
